title: XTP provisioning: LDAP-owned exclusive MI principal binding
summary: LDAP Identity now supplies the trusted resolver required by XtpProvisionIngress: a protected xtp.provision session KEYID is admitted only when current Identity Directory state proves one exclusive MI binding, explicit XTP_PROVISION ACL authority and a stable directory revision fence.
invariants: A protected XTP service key is transport evidence; it is not by itself MI identity authority.
The resolver accepts no principal from request payload or source address; it derives the MI principal from current Identity Directory key ownership.
service:xtp.provision, resource:xtp.provision, the client principal, key set and MI principal must all be current and ACTIVE where their lifecycle requires ACTIVE.
The key generation must be current ACTIVE or RETIRING XTP_ENCRYPT material inside its validity window and preserve the same owner/subtree relationship used by XtpLdapKeySource.
A service-wide shared key or more than one current service binding for the KEYID fails KEY_NOT_EXCLUSIVE.
The semantic MI principal must be an ACTIVE NODE or WORKLOAD id beginning mi: and must have explicit ALLOW for XTP_PROVISION on resource:xtp.provision.
The Identity Directory revision is sampled before the decision and must remain unchanged through it; FENCE_REVISION is a local revocation/ACL fence, not a distributed leader-election epoch.
Key revocation, principal revocation or ACL withdrawal fails closed on the next admission decision.
XTP remains cryptographic/session authority; LDAP remains identity/ACL authority; XTP route publication remains effect/commissioning authority.
